clue.text: Appropriate clothing qualities

parts.note: appropriate means proper, fitting
ties are items of clothing worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A dress-code remark about what kind of clothes suit an occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' tempts a solver to look for one word wrapped round another, but here it is just a garment word supplying the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties are the characteristic attributes or traits of something, its qualities.

clue.text: Kitty wrapping large parcel

indicators.note: wrapping means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a kitty is a shared fund or pot

explanation.surface: A cat curled round a big package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcel' is a parcel of land, not a package.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small piece of land, a parcel.

clue.text: Nasty old couple of females pondering leaving Portugal

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so a couple of them is FF

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: pondering means deep in thought, pensive
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Two unpleasant old women brooding about emigrating from Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: P (Portugal) leaves PENSIVE to give ENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive means unpleasant or causing offence, nasty.

clue.text: Troublemaker cut head off bloomer

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the first letter

parts.note: a terror is an unruly troublemaker, especially a child

explanation.surface: A vandal beheading flowers in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' is a blunder, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British informal word for a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Staff supporting little swimmer in pool

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the staff sits beneath the other piece

parts.note: a tad means a little bit
a staff is a pole

explanation.surface: A rod holding up a small child learning to swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a young frog swimming in ponds, a larva of an amphibian.

clue.text: Former lover sat bare

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed

explanation.surface: An ex-partner modelled nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exposed is uncovered and open to view, laid bare.

clue.text: Purchase bag

explanation.surface: A shopper buying a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a secure hold (purchase) and a holdall go by this short word.

clue.text: Plump dog with new lead

indicators.note: the lead is the first letter, swapped for another one

parts.note: a hound is a dog

explanation.surface: A fat dog being walked on a new leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is the opening letter, not a leash: H becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and round both describe a full, rounded, chubby figure.

clue.text: Falsely claiming Macron's ready with resolution

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is French, and the French for ready is pret
the resolution of a story is its ending

explanation.surface: The French president lies about having a ready solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending is making a false show or claim of something.

clue.text: You and I perhaps harass poor nuns

indicators.note: to harass is to disturb or trouble, so the letters of poor nuns are disrupted

explanation.surface: An accusation that we pester impoverished nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You and I' look like the subject of 'harass' but are examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: You and I are examples of personal pronouns, words standing for nouns.

clue.text: Flipping poor effort, to an extent for volunteer

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the letters found are read backwards
to an extent means only part of the words poor effort is used, letters hidden inside them

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about a feeble attempt by someone who offered to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild curse, but it signals reversal: REFFO, hidden in 'poor effort', is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward unasked, to offer it.

clue.text: Deviation put reader off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of put reader are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone straying from the norm discouraged a reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is the anagram signal applied to PUT READER.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure from a plan or norm is a deviation from it.

clue.text: Titanic no more at sea — guy's oddly forgotten

indicators.note: at sea means confused or adrift, so the letters of no more are mixed up
the odd-placed letters of guy's are dropped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: A lament that the great liner is lost at sea and its man forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the ship but is the adjective meaning huge. ENORMO is the anagram of NO MORE; dropping the odd letters of GUYS leaves US.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic in lower case means gigantic, of colossal size.

clue.text: Jog with no clothes on, entertaining girl primarily

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: with no clothes on means nude

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of girl is taken

explanation.surface: A naked jogger keeping a girl company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like running but means a gentle push. G (first of 'girl') goes inside NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a light push or prod.

clue.text: Engineer spies chap's heavenly transport

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or rearrange it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tech worker spies on someone's celestial vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceships carry travellers through the heavens, the skies above.

clue.text: Reserved archbishop has a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its middle letter, is replaced by another

parts.note: an archbishop is a primate, a senior bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric known for reticence alters his opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The central M of PRIMATE is changed to V. 'Change of heart' looks like a change of mind but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reserved is kept for particular people, not public: private.

clue.text: New tap due — it's bent

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: it's is read as it plus is, the is joining fodder to definition

explanation.surface: A plumber: a replacement tap is needed because the old one is twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like 'twisted' but is the noun meaning natural talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is a natural talent or inclination for it.

clue.text: Weather-beaten, perhaps, after day on a trip?

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a weather-beaten face is an example of a rugged one

explanation.surface: A sunburnt traveller after a day's excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' is the drug-induced sort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tripping is high on hallucinogens, having been given or taken drugs.

clue.text: PM's satisfied southern accent

definitions.note: PM is: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: satisfied means pleased, glad
a tone of voice is an accent or inflection

explanation.surface: A prime minister is content with his southern way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Victorian Liberal Prime Minister four times over.

clue.text: Established faith embracing a cult, finally

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so other letters go within

parts.note: a creed is a religious faith or set of beliefs

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of cult is used

explanation.surface: An old religion that came to absorb a sect.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus T, the last letter of 'cult', sits inside CREED.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to found or set it up, to create it.

clue.text: Volume lost from TV and it's faulty remote

indicators.note: faulty means not working properly, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lost from means the letter is removed from the following words

explanation.surface: The TV's volume has gone because the remote control is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing V from TV AND ITS leaves TANDITS, which 'faulty' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far away, distant in place or time.

clue.text: Is district attorney in uproar showing contempt?

indicators.note: in means the two short pieces sit within the noise, enclosed by it

parts.note: a din is a loud uproar
DA is the US abbreviation for district attorney

explanation.surface: A courtroom question: is the prosecutor scornful amid the commotion?
explanation.walkthrough: A district attorney (DA) is an American public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is the feeling that someone is unworthy, scorn.

clue.text: Most profound flower problem

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee
a pest is a nuisance or problem

explanation.surface: A gardener's deepest worry about blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river (that which flows): the Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean profound or serious, so the superlative is most profound.

clue.text: Quarrel about river fish

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Anglers squabbling over a fish caught in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Strange first half of barn dance

parts.note: rum is British informal for strange or odd

indicators.note: the first half of the word barn is its first two letters

explanation.surface: An odd opening to a barn dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Second insignificant international match is most pleasant

parts.note: wee means tiny, insignificant
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A sports fan rates a minor second fixture the nicest.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means pleasant or delightful, so its superlative is the most pleasant.

clue.text: Empty the motorway and work up speed

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear the motorway and accelerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace or rate of movement, especially of music.

clue.text: Cover your sandwiches well

indicators.note: the words cover your sandwich the answer, holding it between them

explanation.surface: Advice to wrap your lunch carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Very and well are both intensifiers, as in very good or well good.

clue.text: Near this writer is umpire

parts.note: this writer is the setter, so this writer is means I am, I'M
to umpire is to arbitrate, mediate

explanation.surface: The setter introduces himself as the referee nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means close at hand, in the nearest position or time.

clue.text: Sculptor's low energy after runs

definitions.note: the sculptor is: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: after means energy follows runs

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An artist is drained of energy after a bout of diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's call, not 'depressed'. Henry Moore was a famous English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore was an English sculptor known for large bronze reclining figures.

clue.text: Go crazy on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone loses their mind on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to have a stab, an attempt.

clue.text: Paper perhaps still delivered

indicators.note: delivered as a speech is delivered, so this is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: still means not moving, stationary

explanation.surface: A newspaper still turns up on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a paper round but signals a homophone: STATIONARY sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is an example of stationery, office and writing materials.
